task.title: M10: Runtime trace capture harness for Capacitor (browser via CDP, Bun server via preload), no changes to the app repo
task.description:
POC of capturing which files and file-to-file edges are exercised while the Capacitor app (~/source/ao/capacitor-app) is used, without modifying that repo. Capacitor is a Bun 1.3.11 app: Bun.serve in src/index.tsx bundles the React SPA (src/frontend.tsx) and hosts a small server side (MCP handler, llms.txt); most logic runs in the browser and talks to Supabase. Prod and staging run on Render with startCommand 'bun run start'. Two capture paths, both verified to work with zero repo changes:

1. Browser (the bulk of the code). A 'codeviz trace' command drives Chrome through the DevTools Protocol (Playwright, dev dependency of codeviz only): open the app URL (local dev server, staging, or prod), start Profiler precise coverage with call counts, poll takePreciseCoverage every ~500 ms, and also run the CDP sampling profiler for stacks. Map bundle URLs back to src/ paths through the served source maps (Bun dev mode and 'bun build --sourcemap' emit them; check whether the Render prod build serves .map files and, if not, run against staging or a local production build). Precise coverage deltas give per-file, per-function counts per tick; adjacent stack frames in different files give file->file runtime edges per tick. A '--attach <port>' mode connects to a Chrome started with --remote-debugging-port so Dylan can click around in his own browser instead of a scripted session.

2. Bun server. Zero-touch via BUN_OPTIONS="--preload=<harness>/bun-trace.ts" (works on 1.3.11; can be set as a Render env var without touching render.yaml). The preload registers a Bun.plugin onLoad for the app's src/**/*.ts(x) that injects a per-function entry counter and a lightweight caller-file capture (Error stack top frame, sampled 1 in N) and posts aggregated deltas to the codeviz collector endpoint every second. A recorded alternative for local runs is 'bun --cpu-prof' (writes a Chrome .cpuprofile with original src/ paths on exit); parse it into the same format.

Output: a trace file (JSON lines, gzip) in a generic time-series shape that extends the M8 overlay format: header {repoId, sha, startedAt, tickMs, source: browser|server}, then one record per tick {t, files: [[path, calls]], edges: [[from, to, calls]]}. The SHA comes from the running build (git rev-parse for local, a header or build info for Render; if unavailable, the user passes --sha). Live mode: the harness streams ticks over a websocket or long-poll to codeviz serve, which fans them out to the UI (consumed by the M10 trace view story).

Acceptance criteria:
- 'codeviz trace browser <url> --out trace.jsonl.gz' against the local Capacitor dev server (bun run dev) produces a trace in which navigating Makers -> Action Items -> Settings yields distinct sets of src/pages/* and src/components/* files per tick, and at least one runtime edge between a page file and a hook or lib file.
- 'codeviz trace browser --attach 9222' works against a user-driven Chrome session.
- Server capture via BUN_OPTIONS preload produces ticks naming src/server/* files when the MCP endpoint is hit, with no file in capacitor-app modified (git status clean after the run); overhead measured and printed at the end of the run.
- '--cpu-prof' import: 'codeviz trace import-cpuprofile <file>' converts a Bun or Chrome .cpuprofile into the same format.
- Paths in the trace are repo-relative and match the paths in the snapshot for the same SHA; unmatched paths (node_modules, bundler runtime) are counted and reported, not included.
- Never writes into the analyzed repo; harness files live in codeviz. One test for the cpuprofile parser and the sourcemap path mapping; no new runtime dependencies in the CLI beyond what trace needs (Playwright is dev/optional).
